title: 1. Hook: A Rainy Day Surprise!
text: Imagine it is raining heavily outside. You and your friends wanted to play in the park, but now you are stuck at home. What will you do to have fun?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Think About It...
text: Why do we play some games inside the house, like Ludo, and some outside, like Cricket? What makes them different?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Inside vs Outside
content.description: Notice how some games need a small board, while others need a huge playground!

title: 4. Reveal: Indoor and Outdoor Games
text: Games that we play inside a room or a house are called Indoor Games (like Chess and Carrom). Games that we play in an open ground or park are called Outdoor Games (like Football and Cricket).

content.definition: Games played inside a building or house.
Games played outside in open spaces or playgrounds.

content.question: Which of the following is an outdoor game?

title: 6. Reflection: Your Turn to Reflect
text: Close your eyes and think about your absolute favorite game. Is it an indoor game or an outdoor game? Why do you like it so much?

title: 7. Connection: Connecting the Dots
text: Did you know that outdoor games make our muscles strong, while indoor games like chess make our brain sharp? We need both to grow healthy!

content.title: 8. Mastery: Game Detective
content.description: Take a piece of paper and write down the names of 5 indoor games and 5 outdoor games that you or your friends play.

title: 1. Hook: A Trip to the Past
text: Look at the mobile phone or computer you are using right now. Did your grandparents have these when they were your age? How did they play?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Curious Minds
text: If there were no video games or mobile phones, what kind of games do you think children played in the past?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Hopscotch (Stapu)
content.description: A classic game played by drawing boxes on the ground and hopping through them.

title: 4. Reveal: Traditional Games
text: Before modern toys, children played traditional games like Hopscotch (Stapu), Hide and Seek (Chhupan Chhupai), Seven Tiles (Pitthu), and Marbles (Kancha). These games are simple and lots of fun!

content.tip: Encourage students to ask their grandparents about the rules of games like 'Gilli Danda' or 'Pitthu'.

content.mistake: Thinking that old games are boring.
content.correction: Traditional games are actually very active and can be played with many friends using simple things like stones or a piece of chalk!

content.question: What is another name for the game 'Stapu'?

title: 6. Reflection: Reflect and Ask
text: Talk to your parents or grandparents tonight. Ask them what their favorite game was when they were your age. You might be surprised!

title: 7. Connection: The Nature Connection
text: Traditional games often don't need expensive toys. They use things around us, like stones, sticks, or just a safe open space. They connect us to nature and each other.

content.title: 8. Mastery: Learn a New Old Game
content.description: Learn the rules of one traditional game from an elder in your family. Teach it to your friends and play it together this weekend!
